title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: Price increase (4.1%)
drivers.evidence: Same price in 2026-09-28–2026-10-05: sales averaged 24.0 vs baseline 25.3 (x0.95). Recent drop suggests sensitivity. Noise-adjusted effect at this price is ~x0.83, but limited data.

drivers.name: Supply delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates potential stockout. No historical data on delivery warnings, but supply risk typically reduces demand. Conservative estimate; evidence is anecdotal.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 25.3. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 4.1% to $13.93, a level seen in recent weeks (2026-09-28 to 2026-10-05) with sales dropping to 27–21 units (x0.83–0.83 vs baseline). This suggests a price sensitivity effect. Supplier delivery warning adds supply risk, likely reducing demand. Historical price increases (e.g., 2026-09-28) show no lift; past promotions at lower discount levels had noise-adjusted lifts near 1.0. No evidence of post-promo dip. Combine price and supply risk: downward adjustment. Evidence is limited (one price point, one warning), so shrink toward 1.0. Final median multiplier shrunk to 0.85.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
